transcript:
Practitioner: This is your initial assessment, Mr Bennett. Can you tell me what happened?
Mr Bennett: I'm 82. I fell in the kitchen on the 3rd of March and ended up on ward 7 at the General for a week.
Joan (wife): We've been married 54 years. I can't lift him any more.
Practitioner: What support would help now you're home?
Mr Bennett: Two visits a day. A morning one around nine, half an hour, and one at tea time, about half five, fifteen minutes.
Practitioner: What did you enjoy doing before?
Mr Bennett: I was a joiner for forty years. I still like making bird boxes in the shed.
Practitioner: And before the fall, how did you manage?
Mr Bennett: I drove us to the shops every week and did all the garden myself.
Practitioner: What can you do now?
Mr Bennett: I can get about the house with my frame and make my own breakfast. Joan has to help me with my socks.

form.reason:
Mr Bennett is 82 and lives with his wife Joan; they have been married 54 years. He fell in the kitchen on 3 March and was admitted to ward 7 at the General for a week. Joan reports she can no longer lift him.

Times requested as followed -

Morning visit - Around 9am (30 minute visit)
Lunch visit - Around 13:00pm (15 minute visit)
Tea visit - Around 17:30pm (15 minutes)

transcript:
Practitioner: This is a review of your package of care, Mrs Okafor.
Daughter: Mum isn't eating properly. Half her meals come back.
Mrs Okafor: That's not true, I eat fine. I just don't like the frozen dinners.
Practitioner: What did you enjoy doing, what skills do you have?
Mrs Okafor: I worked in the hospital canteen for twenty years. I love cooking for the family.
Practitioner: How independent were you before?
Mrs Okafor: I did everything myself, the cooking, the cleaning, the bus into town.
Practitioner: And now?
Mrs Okafor: I can wash and dress myself if I take my time. My daughter does the shopping.

transcript:
Practitioner: This is an initial assessment. What made you get in touch, Mr Price?
Mr Price: My breathing has got worse and the stairs are hard now.
Practitioner: What did you enjoy, what skills do you have?
Mr Price: I sang in the male voice choir for thirty years.
Practitioner: How did you manage before?
Mr Price: I looked after my grandchildren every day after school, and I walked the dog twice a day.
Practitioner: What can you do now?
Mr Price: I can still walk to the end of the road with a rest. My son brings my shopping.
